clue.text: Fish with rod

definitions.meaning: a common freshwater fish with spiny fins
an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a freshwater fish, and the old measure of length equal to a rod or pole.

clue.text: Officer, having to investigate around Salisbury, turned up before board

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the piece is read from bottom to top
around tells us that the snooping word goes round the statesman's name

parts.note: to snoop is to pry into or investigate
Robert Cecil, Marquess of Salisbury, was a Victorian Prime Minister
a table, as in the meals provided (board and lodging)

explanation.surface: A policeman, sent to look into something around Salisbury, ends up facing a disciplinary board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the snooping word round the statesman, and 'turned up' reverses that whole container in this down clue; 'before' sets it ahead of the board word. Lord Salisbury's family name was Cecil.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is the lowest-ranking police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Plump for some toast

definitions.meaning: plump means ... or chubby in shape
a ... of toast is one slice

explanation.definitionFit: Round means chubby, as plump does, and a round of toast is a slice or serving of it.

clue.text: House in which, delighted, one is put up by foreign gentleman

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces go inside the house abbreviation
in a down clue, put up means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: glad means pleased or delighted
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A foreign gentleman puts up a happy guest in his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the happy word plus one, giving IDALG, and 'in which' sets that inside the house abbreviation. 'delighted' reads as describing the guest but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman of the lower ranks, so a gentleman from abroad.

clue.text: Get pardon sorted out for sponsor

indicators.note: sorted out suggests these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks a sponsor to arrange a pardon for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges the letters of GET PARDON.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent stands sponsor for a child at its baptism, a role the church calls sponsor.

clue.text: Song penned by 27

indicators.note: penned by means the song sits enclosed within the answer to 27

explanation.surface: A song written by whoever is at clue 27.
explanation.walkthrough: The 27 is 27 across, EAGLE-EYED; the word sits inside its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song for three or more voices, popular in the 18th century.

clue.text: Look certain to support record being broadcast

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
lo is an old word for look
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone sure a recording will go out on air checks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts LO + SURE below DISC, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclosure is making something known publicly, close to news being spread or broadcast.

clue.text: A chorus rendered in The Bull

indicators.note: rendered means performed or made into something else, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A choir sings in a pub called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges A CHORUS. The Bull reads as a pub name; the definition is just Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurochs was an extinct European wild ox, ancestor of domestic cattle, so a kind of bull.

clue.text: Tom's friend sure to be heading for the orient

parts.note: Harry East is Tom's friend in the novel Tom Brown's Schooldays
bound to be means sure to be

explanation.surface: Tom's friend is certain to travel to the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown's Schooldays is a Victorian novel set at Rugby School, where Tom's best friend is East.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastbound means travelling east, towards the countries of the Orient.

clue.text: Play disrupted — and it's us in court

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a play was interrupted, and now they are the ones being sued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges all of AND IT'S US IN COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Andronicus is Shakespeare's early revenge tragedy.

clue.text: City with strip that's cleaner

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A city with a strip club offers cleaning services.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman who washes clothes and linen, so a cleaner.

clue.text: Took another chance to pass a spider round

indicators.note: round says the spider word goes around the A

parts.note: in snooker a spider is a type of rest for the cue

explanation.surface: Someone retakes an exam about spiders.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and billiards a spider is a raised rest that holds the cue over other balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit an exam is to take it again in a second attempt at passing.

clue.text: Old king welcomed divine baby

indicators.note: welcomed means took in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme
a divine is a clergyman, and DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: An ancient king receives a heavenly infant.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to pamper and overprotect them, as coddling does.

clue.text: Inactive drugs knock back old boy in some situations

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the other

parts.note: places means situations or locations

indicators.note: knock back means the piece is turned back to front

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Drugs that do nothing are knocked back by an old man in some cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' makes the old boy read BO, and 'in' sets it among the situations. 'knock back' tempts as drinking pills, fitting the drugs surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Placebos are dummy medicines with no active ingredient, given for psychological effect or in trials.

clue.text: Plot employing tricks and plagiarism

parts.note: cons are tricks or swindles
piracy is copying someone's work without permission

explanation.surface: A scheme using deceit and stolen ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group to do something wrong, a plot.

clue.text: Conservative and Labour leaders passionate and vociferous

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the two party names

parts.note: amorous means passionate in love

explanation.surface: The heads of the two main parties are heated and loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous means noisy and insistent, the same as vociferous.

clue.text: Being equivalent to gunman, I will have been trained

indicators.note: trained means disciplined into new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gunman says his training is as good as any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will have been trained' rearranges TO GUNMAN I; 'to' is part of the fodder, not of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounting, as in amounting to, means adding up to or being equivalent to.

clue.text: Turn down branch line heading for Newquay

parts.note: a spur is a short branch railway line

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Turning down a branch railway route to the Cornish resort of Newquay.
explanation.walkthrough: Newquay is a seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn something is to reject or turn it down with contempt.

clue.text: Bond retired early, before completion of Goldeneye

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: soon means early or before long

indicators.note: completion of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: James Bond retired early, before finishing the film GoldenEye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses the word for early to NOOS, and 'before' sets it ahead of the film's last letter. Bond is the definition, not the spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop that binds or ties, so a bond in the sense of a tie.

clue.text: Request missing answer following test, for instance

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the test word

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: missing means the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a plea is a request

explanation.surface: An exam asks for something without supplying the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops the answer abbreviation from the request word, and 'following' puts the remainder after the test. 'for instance' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: For instance means by way of example, so the answer is the noun in the phrase.

clue.text: Concede mistake has recurred, in part

indicators.note: in places the reversed error inside the word for part

parts.note: to sunder is to part or separate

indicators.note: recurred is read literally as run back, so the word reverses

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone admits defeat because the same error happened again in one section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has recurred' reverses the mistake to RRE and 'in' sets it inside the word for part. 'part' looks like a noun but is the verb, to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or yield, as conceding does.

clue.text: Description of English Prime Minister after he got in

indicators.note: got in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were both British Prime Ministers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A label given to an English Prime Minister after he was elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in' puts the pronoun inside the Prime Minister's name, giving PITHET, which follows the English abbreviation. Either Pitt, father or son, serves.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase attached to a name, such as the Great.

clue.text: Name covering a member of the Commonwealth

definitions.text: Name covering a member of the Commonwealth

parts.words: Name covering a member of the Commonwealth
parts.note: a country whose very name was coined in 1964 to cover two former British territories, Tanganyika and Zanzibar

explanation.walkthrough: The country's name blends the first letters of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, which united in 1964; both had been in the Commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanzania is an East African republic and a Commonwealth member.

clue.text: Primate, a person of distinction with substantial backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so both pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a nob is a person of high social rank
big means substantial

explanation.surface: An important person is supported by a well-built primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NOB + BIG into GIBBON.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibbons are small long-armed apes of South-East Asia, and apes are primates.

clue.text: Wash black articles together

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Washing dark clothing all in one load.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash, in a bath or by applying water.

clue.text: Pass some bananas

definitions.meaning: to pass something is to give it across to someone
a bunch of bananas growing together on the stalk

explanation.definitionFit: Hand means pass over to someone, and a hand of bananas is one bunch.

clue.text: Start to blow, taking floppy balloon

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: limp means floppy or slack

explanation.surface: Blowing up a floppy balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, a large balloon.

clue.text: I teach PT — a career lacking any interest

indicators.note: to career is to rush wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A PE teacher describes a career that holds no interest for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb (to rush headlong) and rearranges I TEACH PT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no interest, enthusiasm or concern.

clue.text: Keen-sighted golfer's achievement, I would say

parts.note: an eagle is a hole played two under par

indicators.note: say signals that the next piece is heard rather than seen

parts.note: I would is contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: A golfer claims that good eyesight brought about a great score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' says I'D is heard, sounding the same as EYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle-eyed means having very sharp sight, like an eagle's.

clue.text: Don't start to highlight hair

indicators.note: don't start to means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to stress is to highlight or emphasise

explanation.surface: Don't begin putting highlights in your hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.
